B13C001.summary: Yudhishthira, stricken by the war's dead and by Bhishma's wounded body, asks how he can find peace of mind. Bhishma answers with the tale of Gautami, whose son dies of a snakebite, and the fowler Arjunaka, who wants the serpent killed. Mrityu (Death), the serpent and Kala (Time) each deny being the true cause, and Kala concludes that every creature's own karma decides its fate. Bhishma applies the lesson to Yudhishthira's grief, and Yudhishthira is calmed and asks again.

scenes.B13C001S01: A heading, then Yudhishthira's lament over Bhishma's wounds and the war's dead, Bhishma's reply introducing an old tale, and Gautami's plea that the serpent be freed.
scenes.B13C001S02: The fowler insists the serpent must die to ease grief and earn merit, while Gautami argues the death was fated and that forgiveness is better.
scenes.B13C001S03: Gautami keeps refusing, the fowler cites Indra and Mahadeva to justify killing, and the bound serpent speaks, blaming Mrityu for ordering the bite.
scenes.B13C001S04: The serpent argues it is not an independent cause, like one part of a potter's tools, and the fowler rejects that, ending with the priest analogy.
scenes.B13C001S05: Mrityu appears and explains that he and the serpent both act under Kala, who drives all beings, so the serpent asks to be released.
scenes.B13C001S06: The fowler rejects both excuses and vows to kill them, Mrityu says both depend on Kala, and Kala arrives to settle the dispute.
scenes.B13C001S07: Kala says the child's own karma was the cause, Gautami accepts this and asks the fowler to release the serpent, and Bhishma and the frame narration close the episode.

shots.B13C001S01H01: Heading: the Anusasanika Parva section begins.
shots.B13C001S01H02: An opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and the goddess Saraswati.
shots.B13C001S01H03: Yudhishthira says he finds no peace of mind, since he feels he caused the war's deaths and Bhishma's suffering, and asks how he can be cleansed of sin.
shots.B13C001S01H04: Bhishma asks why Yudhishthira blames his own soul, then begins an old tale about Gautami, whose son died of a snakebite, and the fowler Arjunaka, who binds the serpent.
shots.B13C001S01H05: Gautami asks the fowler to free the serpent, since killing it is sinful and would not bring her son back.
shots.B13C001S02H01: The fowler insists on killing the serpent, arguing that revenge is how practical people ease their grief.
shots.B13C001S02H02: Gautami replies that the boy's death was predestined, so the serpent should not be destroyed, and asks the fowler to forgive it.
shots.B13C001S02H03: The fowler argues that killing an enemy earns great merit, as a sacrifice does.
shots.B13C001S02H04: Gautami asks what good comes from tormenting an enemy, and suggests they earn merit by releasing it.
shots.B13C001S02H05: The fowler argues that protecting many from one wicked creature matters more, and tells Gautami to let him kill it.
shots.B13C001S03H01: Gautami repeats that killing the serpent will not restore her son and asks the fowler to release it.
shots.B13C001S03H02: The fowler cites Indra's killing of Vritra and Mahadeva's share of a destroyed sacrifice to urge the serpent's immediate death.
shots.B13C001S03H03: Bhishma says Gautami does not give in, and that the bound serpent, struggling to stay calm, speaks in a human voice.
shots.B13C001S03H04: The serpent says it bit the child only because Mrityu sent it, so any sin lies with Mrityu.
shots.B13C001S03H05: The fowler replies that the serpent, as the instrument of the act, is still guilty and deserves death.
shots.B13C001S04H01: The serpent argues that it is no independent cause, like the potter's wheel and rod, so any fault lies in the whole set of causes.
shots.B13C001S04H02: The fowler says that even a non-prime cause deserves death, and that a doer cannot escape implication in an evil act.
shots.B13C001S04H03: The serpent says no effect comes without an intervening act, so its role should be weighed alone, and any guilt rests on whoever incited it.
shots.B13C001S04H04: The fowler calls the serpent undeserving of life and says it committed an atrocious act by killing the infant.
shots.B13C001S04H05: The serpent replies with the analogy of priests who pour butter into a fire and do not take the sacrifice's merit, so it should not be judged that way.
shots.B13C001S05H01: Bhishma says the serpent has finished speaking as Mrityu directed it to.
shots.B13C001S05H02: Mrityu appears in person and addresses the serpent.
shots.B13C001S05H03: Mrityu says Kala guides both of them, that Kala drives all beings and all things, and so neither is the cause of the child's death.
shots.B13C001S05H04: The serpent says it does not blame Mrityu or fully excuse him, since it only acts under his direction.
shots.B13C001S05H05: Bhishma continues: the serpent asks the fowler to stop binding it, since it has heard Mrityu and is blameless.
shots.B13C001S06H01: The fowler says neither of their words clears them, calls Mrityu cruel, and vows to kill the serpent as well.
shots.B13C001S06H02: Mrityu says he and the serpent are not free agents but depend on Kala and carry out their appointed work.
shots.B13C001S06H03: The fowler asks how pleasure and anger, which come from good and bad deeds, can arise if both of them are dependent on Kala.
shots.B13C001S06H04: Mrityu says everything is done under Kala's influence, so he and the serpent deserve no censure.
shots.B13C001S06H05: Bhishma says that Kala arrives at the scene of this dispute over morality and speaks to all three.
shots.B13C001S07H01: Kala says none of the three is guilty, that the child's own karma was the true cause, and that all beings are bound by their karma.
shots.B13C001S07H02: Gautami accepts that her own past deeds caused her son's death, asks Kala and Mrityu to leave, and asks the fowler to release the serpent.
shots.B13C001S07H03: Bhishma says Kala, Mrityu and the serpent return to their places and Gautami and the fowler are calmed, then tells Yudhishthira to put aside grief, since men go to heaven or hell by their karma and the kings were slain through Kala's acts.
shots.B13C001S07H04: Vaisampayana begins the frame narration, saying Yudhishthira was consoled after hearing all this.
shots.B13C001S07H05: Yudhishthira, now consoled, speaks again and asks Bhishma a further question.

B13C002.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether any householder has ever conquered Death through virtue, and Bhishma tells of Sudarsana, son of Agni, and his wife Oghavati. When Mrityu sends a Brahmana to test Sudarsana's vow of hospitality, Oghavati accepts the guest out of duty, and Sudarsana affirms that honoring a guest is his highest duty. Dharma appears to praise the couple as having conquered Death, and Bhishma concludes that a guest's blessing is worth more than a hundred sacrifices.

scenes.B13C002S01: Bhishma tells of the royal line leading to Sudarsana and Oghavati, whose guest-honoring virtue defeats Mrityu's test, ending with Dharma's praise and Bhishma's lesson for householders.

shots.B13C002S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma whether any householder has ever conquered Mrityu through virtue, and asks for the story.
shots.B13C002S01H02: Bhishma traces the royal line to Duryodhana, whose daughter Agni marries; their son Sudarsana vows to honor every guest, Mrityu tests him through a Brahmana and Oghavati, and Dharma appears to praise him as having conquered Death.
shots.B13C002S01H03: Indra approaches the Brahmana in a chariot, and Bhishma concludes that honoring a guest is the householder's highest duty and that the story brings glory to those who hear it.

B13C003.summary: Yudhishthira asks how Viswamitra, born a Kshatriya, came to be a Brahmana when that status is so hard for the other classes to reach. He lists Viswamitra's feats, including destroying Vasishtha's hundred sons, founding the Kusika line, and rescuing Sunasepha. He contrasts this with Matanga, a Chandala who could not win Brahmanhood, and asks how the change could happen without a new body.

scenes.B13C003S01: Yudhishthira asks how the Kshatriya Viswamitra became a Brahmana, citing his many deeds and comparing his case with Matanga's failure.

shots.B13C003S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how the Kshatriya Viswamitra became a Brahmana, citing his feats and the failure of Matanga, and asks Bhishma to explain how it happened without a new body.

B13C004.summary: Bhishma explains how Viswamitra became a Brahmana, beginning with King Gadhi, whose daughter Satyavati is sought in marriage by the sage Richika. Gadhi asks for a dowry of a thousand horses, which Varuna supplies, and Richika then arranges sacred food for mother and daughter that is meant to decide the sons' castes. Satyavati's mother swaps the portions and trees, Satyavati pleads to keep her own son from being a Kshatriya, and Gadhi's wife bears Viswamitra, who though a Kshatriya by birth becomes a Brahmana and founds many Brahmana lines.

scenes.B13C004S01: Bhishma gives the family history of Gadhi and Richika, the horse dowry, and the swapped sacred food that changes the sons' destinies, ending with Viswamitra's rise to Brahmanahood.

shots.B13C004S01H01: Bhishma begins the account of how Viswamitra became a Brahmana, tracing the royal line down to King Gadhi and his daughter Satyavati, whom the sage Richika seeks.
shots.B13C004S01H02: Gadhi asks Richika for a dowry of a thousand horses, each with one black ear, before he will give his daughter.
shots.B13C004S01H03: Varuna supplies the horses, Gadhi gives Satyavati in marriage, the mother and daughter swap their sacred food and trees, Richika warns the swap will reverse their sons' destinies, Satyavati pleads, and Viswamitra and Jamadagni are born, with Viswamitra's many sons listed and Bhishma concluding the story.

B13C005.summary: Yudhishthira asks about the merit of compassion and the marks of devout men. Bhishma answers with the tale of a parrot named Suka, whose tree is withered by a fowler's poisoned arrow, and who refuses to leave it even as he dies with it. Indra, disguised as a Brahmana, is moved by the bird's constancy, and grants a boon that revives the tree, after which the parrot joins Indra in heaven. The lesson is that companionship with the good brings people the ends they desire.

scenes.B13C005S01: Bhishma tells the story of the parrot Suka and Indra as an illustration of compassion and devout conduct, ending with the moral about companionship.

shots.B13C005S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to describe the merits of compassion and the characteristics of devout men.
shots.B13C005S01H02: Bhishma tells how a fowler's poisoned arrow withers a tree, how the parrot in its hollow refuses to leave it, and how Indra comes in disguise to ask why.
shots.B13C005S01H03: The parrot refuses to desert the tree that raised him, so Indra grants a boon, the tree revives under nectar, and the parrot later joins Indra, a lesson about companionship with the pious.

B13C006.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether Exertion or Destiny is the stronger force in shaping a life. Bhishma tells how Vasishtha put this question to Brahma, and Brahma answers with the image of seed and soil: past deeds (destiny) bear fruit only when joined to present effort. Brahma gives examples of kings and others who fell or rose through their own deeds, and concludes that destiny and exertion together are what work.

scenes.B13C006S01: Yudhishthira's question about Exertion and Destiny is answered by Brahma's reply to Vasishtha, with examples of kings who fell or rose by their own deeds and the Pandavas' recovery of their kingdom through valour.

shots.B13C006S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma which is more powerful, Exertion or Destiny.
shots.B13C006S01H02: Bhishma says the question was once put by Vasishtha to Brahma, whether a life is shaped by present acts or by acts from earlier lives, called destiny.
shots.B13C006S01H03: Brahma answers with the image of seed and soil: destiny is useless without personal effort, idleness brings loss, and even the gods rose through their own deeds.
shots.B13C006S01H04: Brahma gives examples of kings and sages who fell or were restored by their own deeds, notes the Pandavas regained their kingdom by valour, and concludes that destiny joined with exertion is what works.

B13C007.summary: Yudhishthira asks what the fruits of good deeds are, and Bhishma explains that deeds bear fruit in later lives in a similar bodily state. He lists the rewards for hospitality, austerity, fasting and vows, and for honoring father, mother and teacher, and says past deeds follow a person as a calf finds its mother. Vaisampayana closes by reporting that the princes were delighted, and that falsehood in speech brings evil just as improper rites do.

scenes.B13C007S01: Bhishma lists how good deeds bear fruit in later states of life, from hospitality and austerity to honoring one's elders, and Vaisampayana reports the listeners' delight and closes the section.

shots.B13C007S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to explain the fruits of good deeds.
shots.B13C007S01H02: Bhishma explains that deeds bear fruit in similar states of later lives, lists rewards for hospitality, austerity, diet, vows and sacrifice, and says past deeds follow a person as a calf finds its mother.
shots.B13C007S01H03: Vaisampayana reports that the Kuru princes were amazed and delighted, and compares falsehood in speech to rites performed wrongly, which bring evil results.

B13C008.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma whom he honors, whom he likes, and what helps in this world and the next. Bhishma says he most values learned Brahmanas and those who feed them generously, and that he holds Brahmanas dearer than his own kin. He explains why Brahmanas must be served with respect, since their energy and penance can destroy those who anger them, and that Kshatriyas must protect them and the Vedas.

scenes.B13C008S01: Yudhishthira asks whom Bhishma honors, and Bhishma explains his devotion to Brahmanas and why Kshatriyas must protect and serve them.

shots.B13C008S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma whom he honors and likes, what he thinks of in times of affliction, and what helps in this life and after death.
shots.B13C008S01H02: Bhishma says he most cherishes learned Brahmanas and generous givers, values Brahmanas above his own kin, explains why they must be served with reverence, and says Kshatriyas must protect the Brahmanas and the Vedas.

B13C009.summary: Yudhishthira asks what becomes of people who promise a gift to Brahmanas and then fail to give it. Bhishma says such a person's good deeds turn fruitless, and tells of a jackal and an ape, once friends, now reborn as animals, who explain the sins that led to their state. Bhishma concludes that promised gifts to Brahmanas must be kept, because Brahmanas carry a fire-like energy and gifts to them bring the highest heaven.

scenes.B13C009S01: Bhishma says that a broken promise of a gift to a Brahmana makes good deeds fruitless, illustrates this with the jackal and ape tale, and urges that Brahmanas' expectations be met.

shots.B13C009S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what becomes of people who promise a gift to Brahmanas and do not give it.
shots.B13C009S01H02: Bhishma says such a person's hopes and good deeds come to nothing, and tells of a jackal, reborn for failing to give a promised gift, eating carrion while his former friend, now an ape, asks why.
shots.B13C009S01H03: The jackal asks the ape what sin made him an ape.
shots.B13C009S01H04: The ape says he once took fruits that belonged to Brahmanas, so one should never take their property and should keep one's promises to them.
shots.B13C009S01H05: Bhishma says he learned this from his preceptor and from Krishna, and that Brahmanas must not be disregarded, since their raised expectations burn like fire and gifts to them bring the highest heaven.

B13C010.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether teaching a low-born person is blameworthy. Bhishma tells of a Sudra who joins a Himalayan asylum, is taught the rites for the ancestors by a Rishi, and is later reborn as a king who makes that same Rishi his priest. The king keeps laughing at the priest because he remembers their past, and reveals that the priest's teaching cost him his penances. Bhishma concludes that Brahmanas should not instruct the low-born, and that teaching for pay pollutes the teacher.

scenes.B13C010S01: Yudhishthira asks about the fault of teaching the low-born, and Bhishma tells of a Sudra at a Himalayan asylum who is taught rites by a visiting Rishi, then reborn as a king who keeps his former teacher as priest.
scenes.B13C010S02: The king offers the priest a boon, and the priest asks only that the king swear to speak the truth, which the king agrees to.
scenes.B13C010S03: The priest asks why the king keeps laughing at him, the king reveals their former lives and the cost of the teaching, and Bhishma draws the lesson that Brahmanas should not instruct the low-born.

shots.B13C010S01H01: Yudhishthira asks whether teaching someone of low birth brings fault on the teacher.
shots.B13C010S01H02: Bhishma describes a Himalayan asylum full of sages and a Sudra, moved by its holiness, who asks the head ascetic to accept him as a disciple.
shots.B13C010S01H03: The head ascetic says a Sudra cannot take the vows of renunciation, but he may stay and serve the community.
shots.B13C010S01H04: The Sudra builds a hut, lives austerely, and welcomes guests, and a visiting Rishi teaches him the ancestor rites; both are later reborn, the Sudra as a prince who becomes king, and the Rishi as a priest who serves him, and the king laughs at him repeatedly, so the priest asks for a single boon.
shots.B13C010S01H05: The king replies that he will grant the boon and would grant a hundred if asked.
shots.B13C010S02H01: The king says that a single boon is a small request, given how fond he is of the priest.
shots.B13C010S02H02: The king says his affection and respect for the priest mean he refuses him nothing.
shots.B13C010S02H03: The king repeats that there is nothing he cannot give.
shots.B13C010S02H04: The priest asks for only one boon, that the king swear to tell the truth, and not any falsehood.
shots.B13C010S02H05: Bhishma says the king agrees to answer truthfully if he knows the answer, and to say nothing if he does not.
shots.B13C010S03H01: The priest asks why the king laughs at him on every occasion, says it shames him, and demands a true answer.
shots.B13C010S03H02: The king reveals that he was once a Sudra who did penance, that the priest taught him the rites, that the teaching cost the priest his penances, and that this is why he laughs at the reversal of their fortunes; he urges the priest to seek a better birth.
shots.B13C010S03H03: Dismissed from office, the priest gives gifts, does penance, and attains success at the old asylum, and Bhishma concludes that Brahmanas should not instruct the low-born, that teaching for pay pollutes the teacher, and that one should teach only what is right and meritorious.

B13C011.summary: Yudhishthira asks where the goddess of prosperity, Sree, always dwells. Bhishma recounts how Rukmini asked Sree this question in Krishna's presence, and Sree answered that she stays with the diligent, self-controlled, grateful and devout, and avoids the idle, dishonest, ungrateful and quarrelsome. She also describes the women and places she favors and shuns, and finally says she dwells in Narayana, whose presence makes a person grow in righteousness, fame and wealth.

scenes.B13C011S01: Bhishma recounts Rukmini's question to Sree in Krishna's presence and Sree's long reply listing the people, women, places and things where prosperity dwells or does not.

shots.B13C011S01H01: Yudhishthira asks in what kind of man or woman the goddess of prosperity always resides.
shots.B13C011S01H02: The question continues, asking Bhishma, chief of the Bharatas, where prosperity always stays.
shots.B13C011S01H03: Bhishma says Rukmini, mother of Pradyumna, once asked Sree in Krishna's presence which people she favors and which she shuns.
shots.B13C011S01H04: Sree says she stays with the diligent, eloquent, self-controlled, grateful and devout, and avoids the idle, unbelieving, ungrateful, thieving and quarrelsome; she names the good and bad women of a household, the auspicious places and creatures she favors, and says she dwells in Narayana, in whom righteousness is complete.

B13C012.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether man or woman takes greater pleasure in union, and Bhishma answers with the tale of king Bhangaswana. After a sacrifice that Indra dislikes, Bhangaswana is turned into a woman by a magic lake, bears a hundred sons, and later sees them killed in a quarrel that Indra stirs up. When Indra offers her a boon, she chooses to remain a woman, saying women take greater pleasure in union, and Bhishma presents this as the answer to the question.

scenes.B13C012S01: Bhishma tells how the king Bhangaswana, turned into a woman by Indra's trick, bears sons and loses them, and then chooses to remain a woman when Indra offers her a boon, which Bhishma uses to answer Yudhishthira.

shots.B13C012S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma which of man or woman gets greater pleasure from union, and asks for a truthful answer.
shots.B13C012S01H02: Bhishma tells how king Bhangaswana, who performed a sacrifice Indra dislikes, is stupefied by Indra on a hunt and turned into a woman after bathing in a lake, and how Indra later sets her sons against each other, before Indra reveals himself and offers a boon.
shots.B13C012S01H03: The lady says a woman's affection is greater than a man's, so she asks that the sons she bore as a woman be restored to life.
shots.B13C012S01H04: Indra is pleased and offers her a choice of remaining a woman or returning to manhood.
shots.B13C012S01H05: The lady chooses to remain a woman because women take greater pleasure in union, Indra grants her wish and returns to heaven, and Bhishma concludes that woman enjoys greater pleasure than man.

B13C013.summary: Yudhishthira asks how a person should conduct himself to pass well in this world and the next. Bhishma answers that one should avoid ten kinds of wrong action, three of the body, four of speech and three of the mind. He names each of them, and says that good and evil deeds bring their own certain results.

scenes.B13C013S01: Bhishma lists the ten wrong actions to avoid, in body, speech and mind, and notes that deeds bring certain consequences.

shots.B13C013S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how a man should conduct himself and what practices help him pass well in this world and the next.
shots.B13C013S01H02: Bhishma says to avoid ten wrong actions, naming killing, theft and adultery of the body, harsh and idle talk, exposing others' faults and lying of speech, and greed, malice and disbelief in the Vedas of the mind, and that good and bad acts bring sure results.

B13C014.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to recount the names and power of Mahadeva, and Bhishma defers to Vasudeva (Krishna), who alone can speak of him fully. Vasudeva tells how he went to Himavat to win a son for Jambavati and met the sage Upamanyu, whose own childhood longing for milk led him to austerities and a vision of Shiva, who tested him in Indra's form and then granted him boons. Vasudeva then recounts his own vision of Mahadeva with Uma and hymns him, and the chapter presents Shiva as the supreme cause of all gods, creatures and weapons, ending with Shiva offering Vasudeva eight boons.

scenes.B13C014S01: Yudhishthira asks for Mahadeva's names and deeds, Bhishma says only Krishna can tell them, and Krishna agrees to speak.
scenes.B13C014S02: Vasudeva begins his discourse on Mahadeva and recalls his journey to Himavat for Jambavati's sake, where he found the asylum of the sage Upamanyu.
scenes.B13C014S03: Upamanyu tells how his mother taught him about Mahadeva, how he practiced austerities until Indra came to test him, and how he declined Indra's boons and affirmed Mahadeva as the supreme cause, before he describes seeing Mahadeva's weapons and attendants.
scenes.B13C014S04: Upamanyu hymns Mahadeva, who grants him boons, and then Upamanyu tells Vasudeva that Vasudeva too will see Mahadeva.
scenes.B13C014S05: Vasudeva describes his own austerities and his vision of Mahadeva with Uma, then hymns him, and Mahadeva offers him eight boons.

shots.B13C014S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to recite Mahadeva's names and tell of his power.
shots.B13C014S01H02: Bhishma says he cannot fully describe Mahadeva, and that only Krishna, who won Mahadeva's favour through penance at Vadari, can do so.
shots.B13C014S01H03: Vaisampayana says that Bhishma then addressed Vasudeva on the subject.
shots.B13C014S01H04: Bhishma asks Vasudeva to recite the names of Mahadeva as Tandi once did before Brahma, so that the assembled sages may hear them.
shots.B13C014S01H05: Vasudeva replies that even the gods cannot fully know Mahadeva, but he will recite some of his attributes.
shots.B13C014S02H01: Vaisampayana resumes the narration after Vasudeva's words.
shots.B13C014S02H02: Vasudeva begins his discourse on the attributes of Mahadeva.
shots.B13C014S02H03: The discourse concerns Mahadeva, who is endued with the highest intelligence.
shots.B13C014S02H04: Vasudeva purifies himself by touching water before he speaks.
shots.B13C014S02H05: Vasudeva recounts how he went on Garuda to Himavat to win a son for Jambavati, found the asylum of Upamanyu, heard Upamanyu's list of Shiva's past favours to demons and sages, and learned how Upamanyu as a boy longed for milk and was told by his mother to seek Mahadeva.
shots.B13C014S03H01: Upamanyu's mother says Mahadeva is hard to know and promises to describe his many forms.
shots.B13C014S03H02: The mother lists Mahadeva's forms, and Upamanyu then undertakes long austerities until Indra comes and offers him boons, which he refuses in favour of Mahadeva alone.
shots.B13C014S03H03: Indra asks what reason Upamanyu has for his belief.
shots.B13C014S03H04: Indra's question continues, asking why a Supreme Being should be the cause of all causes.
shots.B13C014S03H05: Upamanyu answers with a long argument that Mahadeva is the supreme cause, source of Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra, and then describes seeing Mahadeva on his white bull with Uma, surrounded by gods and his weapons.
shots.B13C014S04H01: Upamanyu hymns Mahadeva under many names, bows, and offers water, and the gods praise him while Mahadeva speaks with a smile.
shots.B13C014S04H02: Mahadeva says he is pleased with Upamanyu, who in turn praises him and asks for knowledge, milk-based food for his kin, and Mahadeva's presence at the asylum.
shots.B13C014S04H03: Mahadeva grants Upamanyu freedom from suffering, youth, fame, an ocean of milk, and companionship after a kalpa, and the asylum is blessed.
shots.B13C014S04H04: Vasudeva says he is amazed and asks Upamanyu whether Mahadeva will show him favour too.
shots.B13C014S04H05: Upamanyu promises that Vasudeva will see Mahadeva within six months and gives him mantras to recite.
shots.B13C014S05H01: Vasudeva describes his initiation and months of austerity, then his vision of Mahadeva with Uma in a cloud, surrounded by Rudras and gods, and Mahadeva's words that Vasudeva is dear to him.
shots.B13C014S05H02: Vasudeva hymns Mahadeva as the source of all things, and Mahadeva says he is pleased and tells Vasudeva to ask for eight boons.

B13C015.summary: Vasudeva tells how, after his vision of Mahadeva, he asked for boons such as firmness in virtue, victory in battle, fame, Yoga and many children. Mahadeva agreed, and Uma added further blessings, including a son named Samva and a household of sixteen thousand wives. Vasudeva reported all this to Upamanyu, who then declared that there is no deity like Sarva.

scenes.B13C015S01: Vasudeva describes the boons he asked of Mahadeva and Uma, then reports them to Upamanyu, who bows and praises Sarva as unequalled.

shots.B13C015S01H01: Vasudeva bows to Mahadeva and asks for virtue, victory, fame, might, Yoga and many children, and Mahadeva agrees; Uma then says Vasudeva will have a son named Samva and offers him eight further boons.
shots.B13C015S01H02: Vasudeva names his requests to Uma, and she grants them, promising him many wives, great affection, beauty, and daily guests at his palace.
shots.B13C015S01H03: Vasudeva says that the god and goddess vanished after granting him boons, and that he told all this to Upamanyu, who bowed to Mahadeva and spoke to him.
shots.B13C015S01H04: Upamanyu declares that there is no deity like Sarva, no greater refuge, no giver of such boons, and no equal in battle.

B13C016.summary: Upamanyu tells how the sage Tandi, after ten thousand years of devotion, saw Mahadeva and praised him in a long hymn that calls him the source, end and highest truth of all things. Mahadeva, pleased, grants Tandi indestructibility, knowledge and a son who will write Sutras, and Tandi later passes on a thousand names of Mahadeva, first recited by Brahma. Upamanyu now offers these names to Krishna as an aid to his spiritual progress.

scenes.B13C016S01: Upamanyu recounts Tandi's long devotion, his hymn to Mahadeva, Mahadeva's boons, and how Tandi passed the names of Mahadeva on to Upamanyu.

shots.B13C016S01H01: Upamanyu begins the story of Tandi, who worshipped Mahadeva for ten thousand years, and then beheld him and fell into wonder at his unknowable nature.
shots.B13C016S01H02: Tandi's long hymn calls Mahadeva the holiest of holies, the source and end of everything, the forms of the gods and the elements, and the one sought by Vedas, sacrifice and Yoga.
shots.B13C016S01H03: Upamanyu says Mahadeva, with Uma beside him, is gratified by Tandi's praise, and Tandi has said that not even Brahma or Vishnu can know him.
shots.B13C016S01H04: Mahadeva grants Tandi indestructibility, fame, knowledge, and a son who will write Sutras, and Tandi asks only that his devotion remain steady.
shots.B13C016S01H05: Upamanyu says that Mahadeva then vanished, that Tandi came to his asylum, and that Tandi passed on the thousand names of Mahadeva, first recited by Brahma, which Upamanyu now offers to Krishna.

B13C017.summary: Upamanyu recites the thousand-and-eight names of Mahadeva as an essence of Brahma's ten thousand names and of Tandi's hymn, which is said to cleanse all sin and lead to the highest end. He traces the transmission of this hymn from Brahma through Sakra, Mrityu, the Rudras, Tandi, Sukra, Gautama, Manu, Narayana, Yama, Nachiketa and Markandeya, and then gives it to Krishna. Krishna closes by saying that daily recitation for a year brings the fruit of a horse-sacrifice and protection from demons and snakes.

scenes.B13C017S01: Upamanyu recites the thousand-and-eight names of Mahadeva as a condensed hymn, praises its power to cleanse sin, and traces its line of transmission down to himself and Krishna.
scenes.B13C017S02: Krishna states the reward for reciting the hymn with a pure heart for a whole year.

shots.B13C017S01H01: Vasudeva says that Upamanyu, joining his hands in reverence and concentrating, began to recite the abstract of Mahadeva's names from the beginning.
shots.B13C017S01H02: Upamanyu presents the hymn as an essence of Brahma's ten thousand names, which cleanses sin like the four Vedas, calls Mahadeva Eternal Brahman, and starts a long list of his names as a series of 'thou art' phrases.
shots.B13C017S01H03: A section heading, 'Section XVIII,' appears in the text at this point.
shots.B13C017S01H04: The list of names continues, describing Mahadeva as the source of the Vedas, the bearer of Ganga, the husband of Uma, a boar and horse-headed incarnation, and the maker of many forms.
shots.B13C017S01H05: Upamanyu says the hymn has been praised by Tandi and brings Emancipation and heaven, then traces its line of transmission from Brahma through Sakra, Mrityu, the Rudras, Tandi, Sukra, Gautama, Manu, Narayana, Yama, Nachiketa and Markandeya, and gives it to Krishna.
shots.B13C017S02H01: Krishna says that one who recites the hymn for a year with a pure heart, self-control and chastity gains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice and is safe from demons, spirits and snakes.

B13C018.summary: The Island-born Krishna urges Yudhishthira to recite the thousand-and-eight names of Mahadeva, and a line of sages then describe how Mahadeva rewarded their devotion with knowledge, forgiveness, weapons, sovereignty or the return of lost merit. Galava recounts how Mahadeva brought him safely home to his father, and Krishna repeats Upamanyu's teaching that devotion to Mahadeva frees even sinners. Krishna closes by saying that reciting the hymn for a month earns the merit of a horse-sacrifice and benefits every class.

scenes.B13C018S01: A series of sages, Jaigishavya, Garga, Parasara and Mandavya among them, each tell how Mahadeva rewarded their worship, after the Island-born Krishna and Vasudeva have urged the hymn's recitation.
scenes.B13C018S02: Galava tells of Mahadeva's help in reuniting him with his father, and Krishna then repeats Upamanyu's teaching and concludes with the merit of reciting the hymn.

shots.B13C018S01H01: The Island-born Krishna urges Yudhishthira to recite the hymn, and then Kapila, Charusirsha, Valmiki, Jamadagni's son, Viswamitra, Asita-Devala, Gritsamada and Vasudeva each describe the favours Mahadeva gave them for devotion, such as knowledge, a hundred sons, cleansing from sin, weapons, Brahmanhood, restored merit, release from a curse, and boons.
shots.B13C018S01H02: Jaigishavya says that Mahadeva gave him the eight attributes of sovereignty at Varanasi.
shots.B13C018S01H03: Garga says that Mahadeva gave him knowledge of Time and a thousand learned sons, and extended his life to ten million years.
shots.B13C018S01H04: Parasara says that Mahadeva promised him a son named Krishna, who would arrange the Vedas and be reckoned among the seven Rishis.
shots.B13C018S01H05: Mandavya says that, though wrongly impaled for theft, Mahadeva freed him, promised him long life and heaven, and then vanished with his attendants.
shots.B13C018S02H01: Galava says that, when his mother lamented that his father would never see him again, Mahadeva promised that father, mother and son would be spared death, and Galava found his father alive and embraced him.
shots.B13C018S02H02: Vaisampayana says that Yudhishthira was amazed at these accounts, and that Krishna spoke again to him.
shots.B13C018S02H03: Krishna quotes Upamanyu, who says that sinners cannot reach Isana while devotees, even worms and birds, are freed from rebirth through devotion to Mahadeva.
shots.B13C018S02H04: Krishna recites a long list of the powers and beings that arose from the Creator and says that reciting the hymn for a month earns the merit of a horse-sacrifice, and brings benefit to each of the four classes and a heavenly reward.

B13C019.summary: Yudhishthira asks what the saying about performing all duties jointly in marriage means, since spouses die at different times and women are called false by the ordinances. Bhishma answers with the story of the sage Ashtavakra, who asks the sage Vadanya for his daughter Suprabha and is sent on a long northern journey first. On the way he passes through Kuvera's realm, spends a year of dance and music without noticing, and reaches a golden mansion, where an aged woman urges him to lie with her and he wonders whether she was made ugly by a curse.

scenes.B13C019S01: Yudhishthira asks about the meaning of joint marital duties, and Bhishma begins the story of Ashtavakra, who is sent by Vadanya on a northern journey before he can marry Suprabha.
scenes.B13C019S02: Ashtavakra travels to Kuvera's realm, passes a year in dance and music unaware, reaches a golden mansion, and is pressed by an aged woman to lie with her.

shots.B13C019S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what the saying about performing all duties together in marriage means, given that spouses die at different times and women are called false in the scriptures.
shots.B13C019S01H02: Bhishma tells how Ashtavakra asks the sage Vadanya for his daughter Suprabha, and Vadanya agrees on condition that Ashtavakra first travels to the sacred north.
shots.B13C019S01H03: Ashtavakra asks what he will see there and says he will obey.
shots.B13C019S01H04: Vadanya describes the route past Kuvera's realm to the Himavat plateau of Rudra, where Uma once practised austerities, and tells him to honour a female ascetic in a blue forest on his way back.
shots.B13C019S01H05: Ashtavakra agrees to the journey and asks Vadanya to keep his own word.
shots.B13C019S02H01: Ashtavakra bathes in the sacred Vahuda, reaches Kuvera's realm, and is entertained with dance and music until a year has passed unnoticed; he then moves north to a golden mansion, where seven maidens appear and an aged woman embraces him and urges him to lie with her.
shots.B13C019S02H02: Ashtavakra refuses to approach another man's wife and says he seeks marriage only for offspring, asking her to desist.
shots.B13C019S02H03: The lady argues that women are driven by desire and seldom devoted to their husbands, and that they wreck families as rivers break their banks.
shots.B13C019S02H04: Ashtavakra asks her to stop, agrees to stay a while, and wonders whether her ugliness is the result of a curse; then he asks her for water for his evening rites.

B13C020.summary: The old woman tends to Ashtavakra's bath with soft hands, and when midnight comes she goes to his bed. Ashtavakra refuses, saying he will not lie with another man's wife, but she insists she is her own mistress, claims to have kept a vow of celibacy as a maiden, and asks him to marry her. Ashtavakra questions why any woman would be independent and resolves to keep his restraint, although he is drawn to her.

scenes.B13C020S01: The old woman tends to Ashtavakra's bath and food, comes to his bed at midnight, and is refused by Ashtavakra on grounds of duty.
scenes.B13C020S02: The old woman claims to be her own mistress and asks Ashtavakra to marry her, and Ashtavakra questions her and resolves to keep his restraint.

shots.B13C020S01H01: Bhishma says the old woman rubs Ashtavakra with fragrant oil and washes him with her soft hands, the night passes unnoticed, he worships the sun at dawn and is served delicious food, and at midnight she leaves her own bed for his.
shots.B13C020S01H02: Ashtavakra says his mind turns from congress with another's wife, and asks her to leave his bed and desist of her own accord.
shots.B13C020S01H03: Bhishma says the lady answers that she is her own mistress and that accepting her would bring him no sin.
shots.B13C020S01H04: Ashtavakra replies that women can never be their own mistresses, as the Creator himself decreed.
shots.B13C020S01H05: The lady says she is tormented by desire and that Ashtavakra will incur sin by refusing her.
shots.B13C020S02H01: Ashtavakra says that many faults drag down the man who follows his desires, that he can control his own inclinations, and asks her to return to her bed.
shots.B13C020S02H02: The lady bows, submits to him, and offers to be his wife, declaring again that she is her own mistress and that any sin will be hers alone.
shots.B13C020S02H03: Ashtavakra asks how she can be her own mistress, since a woman is protected by her father, husband and sons in turn.
shots.B13C020S02H04: The lady says she has kept the vow of celibacy since maidenhood and begs him not to destroy her devotion by refusing to marry her.
shots.B13C020S02H05: Ashtavakra says he is inclined to her but asks whether taking her would go against Vadanya's wishes, wonders why her beauty was hidden by age, and resolves to keep to his restraint and truth.

B13C021.summary: Yudhishthira asks why the lady feared no curse from Ashtavakra and how he returned safely. Bhishma reports that she was the embodiment of the northern quarter, who devised the trial at Vadanya's request, and who promised Ashtavakra a safe return, a chosen bride and a son. Ashtavakra reports his journey to Vadanya, who gives him his daughter Suprabha in marriage, and he settles at his hermitage free from mental fever.

scenes.B13C021S01: Yudhishthira asks how Ashtavakra escaped the lady's power, and Bhishma recounts her explanation of the trial, Ashtavakra's return, and his marriage to Suprabha.

shots.B13C021S01H01: Yudhishthira asks why the lady had no fear of Ashtavakra's curse, and how he came back safely from that place.
shots.B13C021S01H02: Ashtavakra asks the lady how she alters her form, and insists she speak truly before a Brahmana.
shots.B13C021S01H03: The lady says the trial was devised to test him, that she is the embodiment of the northern quarter, that Vadanya sent him so she could instruct him, and that he will return safely, win a chosen bride and have a son.
shots.B13C021S01H04: Ashtavakra returns to Vadanya, rests at home, and reports what he saw in the north, and Vadanya gives him his daughter in marriage.
shots.B13C021S01H05: Ashtavakra takes Suprabha as his wife and lives on at his hermitage, free from mental fever.

B13C022.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma which Brahmanas are proper recipients of gifts, and Bhishma answers that any Brahmana who keeps the duties of his order is worthy, with or without outward marks. Bhishma then recounts what Earth, Kasyapa, Agni and Markandeya say about which givers are purified and which Brahmanas fail, and holds that Truth outweighs a thousand horse-sacrifices. He also covers the Sraddha rites, the marks of Righteousness, the offences equal to Brahmanicide, and which Brahmanas are worth honouring, since one worthy Brahmana can rescue a whole family.

scenes.B13C022S01: Yudhishthira asks who is a proper recipient of gifts, and Bhishma says devotion and keeping one's order's duties make a person worthy, with or without marks.
scenes.B13C022S02: Bhishma says that merit from gods' rites comes through the gods' grace, and the four proper kinds of recipients are described, with the views of Earth and Kasyapa.
scenes.B13C022S03: Agni and Markandeya give their views on learned and truthful Brahmanas, and Bhishma then answers Yudhishthira on Sraddha offerings to celibate Brahmanas.
scenes.B13C022S04: Bhishma lists the marks of Righteousness, warns against giving to hypocrites, and holds that abstaining from honey and meat, along with renunciation, is the highest virtue.
scenes.B13C022S05: Bhishma names the right times for wealth, Righteousness and pleasure, lists offences equal to Brahmanicide and foeticide, and describes the Brahmanas worthy of gifts.

shots.B13C022S01H01: Yudhishthira asks which Brahmanas the wise call proper objects of gifts, and whether those who bear the marks of their order are the ones meant.
shots.B13C022S01H02: Bhishma says gifts are proper for any Brahmana who keeps the duties of his own order, whether or not he bears the marks of a student.
shots.B13C022S01H03: Yudhishthira asks what fault an unpurified person incurs when he gives butter or food with devotion to the twice-born.
shots.B13C022S01H04: Bhishma says devotion cleanses even a person who lacks self-restraint, and does so for all acts, not just giving.
shots.B13C022S01H05: Yudhishthira says Brahmanas hired for rites to the gods need not be examined, but those hired for rites to the ancestors should be checked for conduct and skill.
shots.B13C022S02H01: Bhishma says that the merit of rites for the gods comes through the gods' grace, and recalls Markandeya's teaching that Brahmanas are always devoted to Brahman.
shots.B13C022S02H02: Yudhishthira asks why five kinds of people, a stranger, one learned in his duties, a relative by marriage, an ascetic and a sacrificer, are regarded as proper.
shots.B13C022S02H03: Bhishma says the first three must have purity of birth, devotion, learning, compassion, modesty, sincerity and truthfulness, that the other two need five of these, and introduces the views of four great beings.
shots.B13C022S02H04: The Earth says that every sin dissolves as a clod in the ocean through the three duties of officiating at sacrifice, teaching and receiving gifts.
shots.B13C022S02H05: Kasyapa says that the Vedas, the Sankhya philosophy, the Puranas and high birth cannot save a twice-born man who falls from good conduct.
shots.B13C022S03H01: Agni says that a learned Brahmana who uses his learning to destroy others' reputation falls from righteousness and cannot reach the regions of felicity.
shots.B13C022S03H02: Markandeya says he does not know whether a thousand horse-sacrifices would weigh even half as much as Truth on a scale.
shots.B13C022S03H03: Bhishma says the four great beings then departed.
shots.B13C022S03H04: Yudhishthira asks whether a Sraddha offering is well performed when it is given to celibate Brahmanas who solicit it.
shots.B13C022S03H05: Bhishma says a celibate Brahmana who solicits and eats a Sraddha offering falls from his vow, though the Sraddha itself is not stained.
shots.B13C022S04H01: Yudhishthira says the wise call Righteousness many-ended and many-doored, and asks for the settled conclusions.
shots.B13C022S04H02: Bhishma lists the marks of Righteousness, such as non-injury, truth, forgiveness, compassion, self-restraint and candour, and warns that giving to hypocrites who preach virtue while sinning brings suffering in hell.
shots.B13C022S04H03: Yudhishthira asks what is superior to celibacy, and what the highest mark and purity of virtue is.
shots.B13C022S04H04: Bhishma says abstaining from honey and meat is superior to celibacy, and that self-restraint and renunciation are the best marks and purity.
shots.B13C022S04H05: Yudhishthira asks when one should practise Righteousness, when one should seek wealth, and when one should enjoy pleasure.
shots.B13C022S05H01: Bhishma says to earn wealth first, then practise Righteousness, then enjoy pleasure without clinging to any of them, and lists lying in court, deceiving the king and wronging teachers as equal to Brahmanicide, and harming the king or a cow as equal to foeticide.
shots.B13C022S05H02: Yudhishthira asks which Brahmanas are good, which gifts earn great merit, and which Brahmanas should be fed.
shots.B13C022S05H03: Bhishma says Brahmanas free from anger, devoted to righteousness, truthful and self-restrained are good, that one who knows the four Vedas and six duties is worthy, that one such Brahmana can rescue a whole family, and that a worthy Brahmana should be invited and honoured even from afar.

B13C023.summary: Bhishma gives Yudhishthira the rules for Sraddha offerings: the proper timing, the foods that become the portion of Rakshasas when impure or improperly given, and which Brahmanas may and may not be invited, with the ritual words to be spoken and the sin of falsehood. He then sets out the deeds that send people to hell, such as lying, adultery, robbery and eating without sharing, and the deeds that lead to heaven, such as feeding the needy, charity and honouring parents. The chapter closes his teaching on rites and gifts.

scenes.B13C023S01: Bhishma sets out the rules for Sraddhas: timing, impure offerings that go to Rakshasas, unfit and fit Brahmanas, ritual words for each class, and the sins of falsehood and of eating in the wrong place.
scenes.B13C023S02: Bhishma lists the deeds that send people to hell and those that lead to heaven, and ends his teaching on rites and gifts.

shots.B13C023S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what rules govern the acts performed for the gods and ancestors at Sraddhas.
shots.B13C023S01H02: Bhishma says the rites for the gods are done in the forenoon and those for the ancestors in the afternoon, and lists offerings that become the Rakshasas' portion, such as untimely gifts, food touched by dogs or impure women, and food given without proper rites.
shots.B13C023S01H03: Bhishma lists the Brahmanas who should not be invited to Sraddhas, including outcasts, the diseased, physicians, paid performers, sellers of Soma and of Vedic lore, lenders of money, and those who serve Sudras.
shots.B13C023S01H04: Bhishma lists the Brahmanas who may be invited, such as those who keep the rites and the Gayatri or live by farming, and a well-born Brahmana who takes up arms, while those who turn to trade are excluded, and he gives the words to be spoken by each class.
shots.B13C023S01H05: Yudhishthira asks to whom the offerings to gods and ancestors should be given to earn the greatest reward.
shots.B13C023S02H01: Bhishma says that gifts to needy, ascetic and ruined Brahmanas earn great merit, and then lists deeds that send people to hell, such as lying, adultery, robbery, cheating women, spoiling water and buildings, and eating without sharing.
shots.B13C023S02H02: Bhishma names deeds that lead to heaven, such as honouring Brahmanas, truthfulness, serving parents, founding retreats and towns, feeding and charity, and protecting others, and then ends his teaching on rites and gifts.

B13C024.summary: Yudhishthira asks what makes a person guilty of Brahmanicide without actually killing a Brahmana. Bhishma reports that he once put the question to Vyasa, who answered with a list of such acts. These include refusing alms to an invited Brahmana, ruining a learned Brahmana's livelihood, blocking thirsty cattle, disparaging the Srutis, and robbing or harming the helpless.

scenes.B13C024S01: Yudhishthira asks about indirect Brahmanicide, and Bhishma recounts Vyasa's list of acts that count as such guilt.

shots.B13C024S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to explain the circumstances in which a person becomes guilty of Brahmanicide without killing a Brahmana.
shots.B13C024S01H02: Bhishma says he once asked Vyasa the same question, and Vyasa listed acts that count as Brahmanicide: refusing food to an invited Brahmana on a false pretext, ruining a learned Brahmana's means of living, obstructing thirsty cattle, condemning the Srutis, withholding a daughter from a worthy groom, causing grief to Brahmanas, robbing the blind, lame or simple, and burning hermitages or towns.

B13C025.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma about the merit of visiting, bathing in and hearing about the sacred waters on earth. Bhishma recounts the teaching that Angiras gave to Gautama, a long catalogue of named tirthas with the rewards each brings, such as heaven, the merit of a horse-sacrifice, cleansing from sin including Brahmanicide and foeticide, beauty and power. Angiras closes by saying that this teaching, recited or heard, leads to a good birth and memory of past lives.

scenes.B13C025S01: Yudhishthira asks about the merit of sacred waters, Bhishma explains that Gautama put the question to Angiras, and Angiras lists the tirthas with their rewards.

shots.B13C025S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to speak of the merit of pilgrimage, bathing and hearing about the sacred waters on earth, and to name them.
shots.B13C025S01H02: Bhishma says that Angiras made the list, and that Gautama asked him what merit a bath in these waters brings toward the next world.
shots.B13C025S01H03: Angiras lists the sacred waters across the land and the rewards of fasting and bathing at each, including heaven, the merit of horse-sacrifices, cleansing from sin, beauty and power, and says the teaching, recited or heard, brings a good birth and memory of past lives.

B13C026.summary: Vaisampayana describes the many great Rishis who visit Bhishma on his bed of arrows and then vanish, and Yudhishthira asks which countries, rivers and mountains are most sacred. Bhishma tells of a poor Brahmana who keeps the Sila vow and asks a visiting Rishi the same question, and the Rishi answers that the places along the Bhagirathi Ganga are holiest. The Rishi then praises the Ganga at great length, saying her waters cleanse sin, rescue ancestors and lead to heaven, and Bhishma urges Yudhishthira to honour her too.

scenes.B13C026S01: Bhishma, lying on his bed of arrows, receives a visit from many great Rishis, and Yudhishthira asks which places are most sacred, which Bhishma answers by telling the story of a Brahmana and a visiting Rishi.
scenes.B13C026S02: The Rishi praises the Bhagirathi Ganga at length, and Bhishma urges Yudhishthira to seek her protection, with Vaisampayana noting that hearing the praise cleanses sin.

shots.B13C026S01H01: Vaisampayana describes Bhishma, felled by Arjuna, lying on his bed of arrows and visited by many great Rishis, who converse with him and then vanish while the Pandavas bow to them.
shots.B13C026S01H02: After the Rishis leave, Yudhishthira bows at Bhishma's feet and resumes his questions on righteousness.
shots.B13C026S01H03: Yudhishthira asks which countries, provinces, retreats, mountains and rivers are foremost in sanctity.
shots.B13C026S01H04: Bhishma recounts an old tale of a Brahmana who keeps the Sila and Unccha vows, who hosts a Rishi crowned with success and then talks with him on the Vedas and Upanishads.
shots.B13C026S01H05: The poor Brahmana puts Yudhishthira's question to the Rishi, asking which countries, rivers and mountains are most sacred.
shots.B13C026S02H01: The Rishi answers that the places along the Bhagirathi Ganga are holiest, and praises her at great length: her waters cleanse sin, rescue ancestors, lead to heaven and surpass sacrifices, and even her sight and name bring merit.
shots.B13C026S02H02: Bhishma says the Rishi then rose into the sky, the Brahmana worshipped Ganga and gained success, and he urges Yudhishthira to seek her with devotion.
shots.B13C026S02H03: Vaisampayana says that Yudhishthira and his brothers were delighted, and that reciting or hearing this praise of Ganga cleanses every sin.

B13C027.summary: Yudhishthira asks how a Kshatriya, Vaisya or Sudra can attain the status of a Brahmana. Bhishma tells of Matanga, who was raised with Brahmana rites but was born of a mixed union, and who learns from a talking she-ass that he is in fact a Chandala by birth. Matanga resolves to win Brahmanahood by severe penance, and Indra appears and warns him that a person of impure birth cannot reach that status.

scenes.B13C027S01: Yudhishthira asks how a lower-born person can become a Brahmana, and Bhishma tells of Matanga, whose talking she-ass reveals his mixed birth, and of Matanga's resolve to do penance.
scenes.B13C027S02: Matanga asks Indra for the status of Brahmana through penance, and Indra warns him that the status cannot be won by one of impure birth.

shots.B13C027S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma whether a Kshatriya, Vaisya or Sudra can attain Brahmanahood by penance, by rites or by learning.
shots.B13C027S01H02: Bhishma says Brahmanahood cannot be won directly from the other three orders, but is reached only after many births, and tells of Matanga, a boy raised with Brahmana rites, who beats a she-ass for running to its mother and asks her why he has been rebuked.
shots.B13C027S01H03: The she-ass says Matanga was begotten by a Sudra barber upon a Brahmana woman, so he is a Chandala by birth and not a Brahmana.
shots.B13C027S01H04: Matanga returns home, and his father asks why he came back without gathering the sacrificial requisites.
shots.B13C027S01H05: Matanga says that a person with a stained birth cannot be happy, resolves on the austerest penance, and is approached by Indra, who offers him any boon.
shots.B13C027S02H01: Matanga asks, as his boon, that he may attain the status of a Brahmana by means of his penance.
shots.B13C027S02H02: Indra warns Matanga that the status of a Brahmana cannot be won by one of impure birth, and urges him to abandon the pursuit before he is destroyed.

B13C028.summary: Matanga persists with his penance, standing on one foot for a hundred years, and Indra returns to explain that a person must pass through many lower births before reaching Brahmanahood. Indra describes a long path through the Pukkasa, Sudra, Vaisya and Kshatriya orders and through the lower kinds of Brahmana, each lasting thousands of years. He ends by urging Matanga to ask for some other boon, since the status of Brahmana is beyond his reach.

scenes.B13C028S01: Matanga stands for a hundred years on one foot, and Indra explains the long path of rebirths through lower orders before Brahmanahood, urging him to choose another boon.

shots.B13C028S01H01: Matanga, undeterred by Indra, stands on one foot for a hundred years; Indra returns and explains that a person must pass through the Pukkasa, Sudra, Vaisya and Kshatriya orders and through several grades of Brahmana over immense spans of time before reaching Brahmanahood, and asks Matanga to choose some other boon.

B13C029.summary: Matanga, born to a Chandala mother, spends a thousand years in penance trying to become a Brahmana. Sakra (Indra) tells him that someone of his birth can never reach that status, and Matanga, grieving, pushes his austerities until he collapses. Sakra then grants him other boons, and Matanga dies. The chapter is used to show that Brahmana status is very high and cannot be won by penance alone.

scenes.B13C029S01: Matanga's long penance, Sakra's refusal to grant Brahmana status, and Matanga's bitter reply.
scenes.B13C029S02: Matanga asks for other boons, Sakra grants him fame, Matanga dies, and Bhishma draws the moral.

shots.B13C029S01H01: Matanga refuses Indra's advice and spends a thousand years in penance, standing on one foot.
shots.B13C029S01H02: After another thousand years, Matanga asks Indra why he still has not won Brahmana status.
shots.B13C029S01H03: Indra says a Chandala can never become a Brahmana; Matanga goes to Prayaga and Gaya and penances until he collapses, and Indra catches him.
shots.B13C029S01H04: Indra explains that Brahmana status is out of Matanga's reach, describes its honour and dangers, and asks him to choose another boon.
shots.B13C029S01H05: Matanga protests that Indra is wounding a man already dead, blames his mother for his birth, and asks for some other boon.
shots.B13C029S02H01: Bhishma says Indra again urges Matanga to name a boon.
shots.B13C029S02H02: Matanga asks for the power to change shape, fly, enjoy pleasures, be honoured by Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, and win lasting fame.
shots.B13C029S02H03: Indra grants him fame as the deity of a verse measure and worship from women, then leaves; Matanga dies and goes to a high place, and Bhishma concludes that Brahmana status is high and comes only by birth.

B13C030.summary: Yudhishthira asks how the king Vitahavya became a Brahmana, since Viswamitra did as well. Bhishma tells how Vitahavya's hundred sons overran the kingdom of Kasi, and how Divodasa's son Pratarddana defeated them in battle. Vitahavya fled to the sage Bhrigu, who protected him and made him a Brahmana by his word alone. The chapter ends with the family line from Gritsamada down to Saunaka, which shows the Brahmana descent of this house.

scenes.B13C030S01: Yudhishthira's question, the wars between the Haihayas and the kings of Kasi, Pratarddana's victory, Vitahavya's elevation by Bhrigu, and the genealogy.

shots.B13C030S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how Vitahavya gained Brahmana status, since Viswamitra did too, and whether it came by a boon or by penance.
shots.B13C030S01H02: Bhishma begins the story: Haihaya's hundred sons take Kasi from Haryyaswa and later defeat Sudeva, and Divodasa rebuilds Benares and fights them for a thousand days.
shots.B13C030S01H03: Divodasa loses his army and treasury, flees his capital, and seeks refuge with the sage Bharadwaja.
shots.B13C030S01H04: Divodasa pleads for protection; Bharadwaja arranges a sacrifice that brings a son, Pratarddana, who quickly masters the Vedas and arms and defeats the Vitahavya sons; Vitahavya flees to Bhrigu, and Pratarddana follows him there.
shots.B13C030S01H05: Pratarddana asks for Vitahavya, but Bhrigu says no Kshatriya is in his hermitage; Pratarddana leaves, and Vitahavya becomes a Brahmana by Bhrigu's word. The text then gives the line from Gritsamada through Ruru and Pramadvara to Saunaka.

B13C031.summary: Yudhishthira asks which men in the three worlds deserve reverent worship. Bhishma tells an old story in which Narada worships a large group of Brahmanas, and Krishna asks him whom he honours. Narada names the Brahmanas he reveres by their virtues and says those who keep such virtues escape every calamity. Bhishma closes by urging Yudhishthira to honour the gods, the ancestors, the Brahmanas and guests.

scenes.B13C031S01: Yudhishthira's question, Krishna's question to Narada, Narada's list of revered Brahmanas, and Bhishma's advice to Yudhishthira.

shots.B13C031S01H01: Yudhishthira asks which men in the three worlds deserve reverence and says he never tires of hearing such talk.
shots.B13C031S01H02: Bhishma introduces an old dialogue in which Narada worships many Brahmanas, and Krishna asks whom he is honouring.
shots.B13C031S01H03: Narada names the Brahmanas he honours and lists their virtues, such as penance, Vedic study, self-restraint, charity and hospitality, and says those who keep them cross every calamity.
shots.B13C031S01H04: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira to honour the deities, the ancestors, the Brahmanas and guests, and says this brings a good end.

B13C032.summary: Yudhishthira asks what merit comes from protecting living beings who seek shelter. Bhishma answers with the story of a pigeon chased by a hawk, which takes refuge in the lap of king Vrishadarbha. The hawk demands the pigeon as its food, and the king ends up offering flesh cut from his own body, which the text presents as the highest act of protection. The story ends with the king's reward in heaven and the claim that hearing it cleanses sin.

scenes.B13C032S01: Yudhishthira's question, the pigeon's plea to King Vrishadarbha, the hawk's objection, and the king's first offer of other meat.
scenes.B13C032S02: The hawk's demand for the king's own flesh, the king's sacrifice, his reward in heaven, and the moral for Yudhishthira.

shots.B13C032S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what merit comes from protecting creatures that beg for shelter.
shots.B13C032S01H02: Bhishma tells of a pigeon chased by a hawk that takes shelter in King Vrishadarbha's lap, and the king comforts it.
shots.B13C032S01H03: The hawk argues that the pigeon is its rightful food and that the king's authority does not extend to birds of the sky.
shots.B13C032S01H04: The king is struck with wonder but does not dismiss the hawk's words, and he turns to answer.
shots.B13C032S01H05: The king offers the hawk other meats such as beef, boar, deer or buffalo, and says he will not abandon a creature that sought his protection.
shots.B13C032S02H01: The hawk refuses other meat, says hawks eat pigeons by natural law, and asks for the king's own flesh equal in weight to the pigeon.
shots.B13C032S02H02: The king cuts his own flesh to weigh against the pigeon; the palace grieves, the earth trembles, and the king finally climbs onto the scale. The gods arrive, showers of nectar and flowers fall, and the king rises to heaven. The text then draws its moral and says reciting the story cleanses sin.

B13C033.summary: Yudhishthira asks which act a king should put first to win happiness in this world and the next. Bhishma answers that honouring learned Brahmanas is the foremost duty of a king. He describes the many kinds of Brahmanas, their great power, and the ruin that comes to those who speak against them. He ends by saying that no one can truly defeat the Brahmanas.

scenes.B13C033S01: Yudhishthira's question and Bhishma's long answer on the king's duty to honour and protect the Brahmanas.

shots.B13C033S01H01: Yudhishthira asks which act a king should put first, and which one brings happiness in both worlds.
shots.B13C033S01H02: Bhishma says that worshipping Brahmanas is the king's foremost duty, describes the varied kinds of Brahmanas and their powers, notes that insulting them brings downfall, and ends by saying no one can overcome them.

B13C034.summary: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira that Brahmanas must be honoured because the kingdom's peace and the gods' favour depend on them. He lists the benefits of feeding and supporting them and the defeats of Kshatriyas who fought them. He then gives a dialogue in which the Earth tells Vasudeva (Krishna) that serving Brahmanas cleanses sin and that harming them leads to ruin. Bhishma closes by urging Yudhishthira to honour the superior Brahmanas.

scenes.B13C034S01: Bhishma's case for honouring Brahmanas, the Earth's teaching to Vasudeva on serving them, and Bhishma's closing advice to Yudhishthira.

shots.B13C034S01H01: Bhishma says Brahmanas must be revered and supported, that the kingdom's peace depends on it, and that the Kshatriyas who fought them were defeated; he then introduces a talk between Vasudeva and the Earth.
shots.B13C034S01H02: Vasudeva asks the Earth by what conduct a householder can cleanse all his sins.
shots.B13C034S01H03: The Earth replies that serving Brahmanas cleanses and brings prosperity, fame and self-knowledge, and that speaking against them brings ruin.
shots.B13C034S01H04: Bhishma says Krishna praised the Earth's words and urges Yudhishthira to always worship the superior Brahmanas.

B13C035.summary: Bhishma says Brahmanas are worthy of worship by birth, because they are the mouths of the gods and guides of all creatures. He quotes verses attributed to Brahma that set out the Brahmanas' duties and the rewards of study, sacrifice and self-restraint. He ends by describing their great power and urging the king to honour them with gifts and service. The section closes with a note that the parva continues in another volume.

scenes.B13C035S01: Bhishma's praise of the Brahmanas, Brahma's verses on their duties, and the closing notes of the section.

shots.B13C035S01H01: Bhishma says Brahmanas deserve worship by birth and recites Brahma's verses on their duties, their study and sacrifice, their power, and the need for kings to serve them.
shots.B13C035S01H02: A note says the Anusasana Parva continues in Volume XI.
shots.B13C035S01H03: A heading marks the start of Section XXXVI.

B13C036.summary: Bhishma tells of Sakra (Indra), who visits the Asura Samvara in disguise and asks how he rose above his kin. Samvara credits his respect for Brahmanas and his willingness to learn from them, and he repeats what his father heard from Soma about the power of Brahmanas. Sakra then takes up the same devotion to Brahmanas and gains the chiefdom of the gods. The story is offered as an example of honouring Brahmanas.

scenes.B13C036S01: Sakra's disguised visit to Samvara, Samvara's account of his devotion to Brahmanas and Soma's teaching, and Sakra's rise after taking up the same course.

shots.B13C036S01H01: Bhishma introduces the story: Sakra, disguised as a matted-haired ascetic, visits the Asura Samvara in a plain car.
shots.B13C036S01H02: Sakra asks Samvara how he won leadership over his people.
shots.B13C036S01H03: Samvara says he respects Brahmanas, learns from them, serves them and takes their teaching to heart; he compares them to bees filling honeycomb.
shots.B13C036S01H04: Samvara repeats Soma's teaching to his father: Brahmanas gain success through penance and speech, should study the Vedas, and should not stay idle at home.
shots.B13C036S01H05: Bhishma says Sakra was moved by these words, began to honour Brahmanas, and gained the chiefdom of the gods.

B13C037.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether a stranger, a long-known companion, or a traveller from afar is the best recipient of a gift. Bhishma says all three can be worthy and lists the qualities that make a recipient deserving, such as learning, truthfulness and self-restraint. He condemns quarrelsome and vain Brahmanas and sets out the householder's duties to the gods, sages, ancestors, Brahmanas and guests. The chapter teaches that the worth of the person matters more than how well one knows them.

scenes.B13C037S01: Yudhishthira's question on the choice of recipients, Bhishma's answer on worthiness, and the householder's duties to others.

shots.B13C037S01H01: Yudhishthira asks which kind of person is the best recipient of a gift: a stranger, a long-known companion, or a visitor from far away.
shots.B13C037S01H02: Bhishma says all three are equal in claim, that gifts should not harm one's dependants, and that a newcomer, a familiar person and a distant traveller all deserve gifts.
shots.B13C037S01H03: Yudhishthira agrees that gifts must not break the scriptures, and says the giver must first judge whether the gift will benefit the recipient.
shots.B13C037S01H04: Bhishma lists the qualities of a worthy recipient, condemns quarrelsome and proud Brahmanas, and sets out the householder's duties to the gods, sages, ancestors, Brahmanas and guests.

B13C038.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to describe the nature of women, whom he calls the root of evil. Bhishma tells of Narada questioning the Apsara Panchachuda, who at first refuses to speak ill of her own sex and then does so at Narada's urging. She lists the faults she ascribes to women, including restlessness, a readiness to break restraints, and an inability to be satisfied. The chapter presents these as a view attributed to Panchachuda, and it sets up the next chapter's question about men and women.

scenes.B13C038S01: Yudhishthira's request, Narada's meeting with Panchachuda, and her agreement to answer.
scenes.B13C038S02: Panchachuda's account of the faults she ascribes to women.

shots.B13C038S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to speak about the nature of women, whom he calls the root of evil and very frail.
shots.B13C038S01H02: Bhishma introduces an old story in which Narada meets the Apsara Panchachuda in Brahma's realm and asks her a question.
shots.B13C038S01H03: Panchachuda says she will answer if the subject is within her knowledge.
shots.B13C038S01H04: Narada asks her to explain the disposition of women.
shots.B13C038S01H05: Panchachuda says she cannot speak ill of her own sex, Narada says that speaking the truth is no fault, and she agrees to answer.
shots.B13C038S02H01: Panchachuda lists the faults she attributes to women: they break their restraints, favour any man who courts them, are never satisfied, and were created with these faults.

B13C039.summary: Yudhishthira presses Bhishma with doubts raised by the previous account: why men still attach themselves to women despite their faults, whether women can deceive and sway men, and whether anyone has ever restrained them. He asks Bhishma to explain how men can protect women and whether women can truly be kept within the bounds set by the scriptures.

scenes.B13C039S01: Yudhishthira's series of questions on why men are drawn to women, whether women can be restrained, and whether anyone has managed it.

shots.B13C039S01H01: Yudhishthira asks why men are drawn to women despite their faults, how women are said to deceive men, whether women can be restrained, and whether anyone has ever succeeded in restraining them.

B13C040.summary: Bhishma says women were created by Brahma after the gods feared that humans would become too righteous, and that they were given desire and anger. He then tells how the sage Devasarman, about to leave for a sacrifice, asks his disciple Vipula to guard his wife Ruchi from Indra. Devasarman describes Indra's endless disguises, and Vipula enters Ruchi's body by yoga power so that Indra cannot approach her. The chapter sets up the test of Vipula's devotion.

scenes.B13C040S01: The account of how women were created, and Devasarman's instruction to Vipula to protect his wife Ruchi from Indra.
scenes.B13C040S02: Devasarman's description of Indra's disguises and Vipula's decision to enter Ruchi's body to guard her.

shots.B13C040S01H01: Bhishma says women are sinful and recounts how Brahma created them after the gods feared human righteousness; then he introduces the story of Vipula guarding the wife of his teacher, Devasarman.
shots.B13C040S01H02: Devasarman says he is leaving for a sacrifice, warns that Indra covets his wife Ruchi, and asks Vipula to guard her closely.
shots.B13C040S01H03: Vipula agrees to do so, but as his teacher is about to leave he asks one more question.
shots.B13C040S01H04: Vipula asks what forms Indra takes and what his body and power are like.
shots.B13C040S01H05: Bhishma says the sage Devasarman truly described all of Indra's illusions to Vipula.
shots.B13C040S02H01: Devasarman describes Indra's many shapes; Vipula weighs the options and decides to enter Ruchi's body by yoga power, staying unseen to guard her until his teacher returns.

B13C041.summary: Indra comes to the hermitage in a beautiful form, intending to seduce Ruchi, but finds that Vipula has bound her body and speech from inside. Indra speaks to her, and she is forced to say words Vipula controls, while Vipula watches Indra's approach from within her. When Vipula reveals himself and rebukes Indra, mentioning Gautama's curse, Indra flees in shame. Devasarman rewards Vipula with a boon that he will never fall from righteousness.

scenes.B13C041S01: Indra's visit to the hermitage, Vipula's rebuke of Indra, and Devasarman's reward to his disciple.

shots.B13C041S01H01: Indra takes a beautiful form and enters the hermitage; Vipula sits motionless inside Ruchi, who cannot rise to welcome him, and Indra speaks to her while Vipula controls her words; Indra is shamed, sees Vipula, and fears his curse.
shots.B13C041S01H02: Vipula comes out of Ruchi's body and rebukes Indra, recalls Gautama's curse that gave him his sex-marks, and warns him to respect the Brahmanas and leave.
shots.B13C041S01H03: Indra slips away in shame; Devasarman returns, hears Vipula's account, praises him, and grants him a boon that he will never fall from righteousness.

B13C042.summary: Vipula, after his success, grows proud of his penance. When Devasarman's sister-in-law asks for celestial flowers, Vipula is sent to fetch some and finds them where Ruchi had dropped them. On the road he hears two couples swear oaths naming his fate in the next world, and he searches his conscience and recalls that he never told his teacher about entering Ruchi's body. He then brings the flowers and honours his teacher. The chapter shows that even a just act can leave a hidden fault.

scenes.B13C042S01: Vipula's pride after his penance, the errand for flowers, the oaths overheard on the road, and his realisation of his own fault.

shots.B13C042S01H01: Vipula, proud of his penance, is sent by his teacher to fetch the same flowers that Ruchi's sister wants; he finds them, passes two quarrelling couples and a group of dice players who each swear oaths naming his fate, and at last recalls that he never told his teacher about entering Ruchi's body; he delivers the flowers and honours his teacher.

B13C043.summary: Devasarman greets his returning disciple Vipula and explains that the two couples and the dice players were Day and Night and the six Seasons, who see every hidden deed. Vipula had not told his teacher the whole truth, but Devasarman judges that his protection of Ruchi was proper and sends him to heaven. Bhishma then recounts a lesson he had from the sage Markandeya: women must be guarded, virtuous women are blessed, and men should not become overly attached to them. Only Vipula is said to have protected women successfully.

scenes.B13C043S01: Devasarman's welcome of Vipula, his explanation of the witnesses to Vipula's fault, and the closing lesson Bhishma draws about women.

shots.B13C043S01H01: Bhishma says Devasarman addressed his disciple Vipula on his return from the errand.
shots.B13C043S01H02: Devasarman says he knows how Vipula protected Ruchi, and asks what Vipula saw on his journey.
shots.B13C043S01H03: Vipula asks who the two couples and six men were, since they seemed to know him.
shots.B13C043S01H04: Devasarman explains that they were Day and Night and the six Seasons, who witness every deed; he says Vipula's concealment was a fault, but his protection of Ruchi was proper, so he sends him to heaven. Bhishma adds that he heard this from Markandeya, and that women should be guarded, virtuous women are blessed, men should not be over-attached, and only Vipula protected women.

B13C044.summary: Yudhishthira asks how a father should choose a husband for his daughter, and Bhishma answers at length on marriage. He names the several forms of marriage, separates the righteous forms from the unrighteous, and sets rules on how many wives each caste may take, on suitable ages and on whom a girl may not marry. Yudhishthira then asks whether a dowry alone makes a bride a wife, and Bhishma answers that only the rites of marriage do, recalling his own seizure of maidens for Vichitravirya. The chapter's main point is that the taking of the hand with proper rites creates the marriage.

scenes.B13C044S01: Yudhishthira's question on choosing a bridegroom, Bhishma's account of marriage forms and rules, and Yudhishthira's question about dower and promises.
scenes.B13C044S02: Yudhishthira's question about a rejected dowry suitor, and Bhishma's answer on dower, sale, and the rites that make a marriage.

shots.B13C044S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma whom a father should choose as a husband for his daughter, calling marriage the foremost duty.
shots.B13C044S01H02: Bhishma says the father should judge the groom's conduct, learning and birth before giving his daughter, and describes the Brahma and Gandharva forms of marriage and the Asura form of purchase.
shots.B13C044S01H03: Bhishma describes the Rakshasa form, calls three of the five forms righteous and two not, gives the number of wives each caste may take, and sets rules on marriage ages, unmarried girls, and whom one may not wed.
shots.B13C044S01H04: Yudhishthira asks whose wife the girl becomes when a dower is paid, promised, or simply displayed, or when a suitor takes her hand with rites.
shots.B13C044S01H05: Bhishma says the girl's hand must be given with proper rites and the kinsmen's consent, that a marriage forced on an unwilling girl brings sin, and that a girl promised to another does not make a later marriage wrong.
shots.B13C044S02H01: Yudhishthira asks how a father should act when a more eligible suitor appears after a dower has been accepted from another.
shots.B13C044S02H02: Bhishma says a dower does not make a girl a wife, that such a payment is a price rather than a marriage, and that a promise or a father's declaration is not marriage either.
shots.B13C044S02H03: Bhishma recounts how he seized two maidens for Vichitravirya, and how king Valhika ruled that a wife is made by the proper giving and taking of her hand, not by a sale. Prince Satyavat then answers questions on a dower-giver who dies, a widow's remarriage to a brother-in-law, and the wedding rites that end at the seventh step, concluding with the gift of a maiden with water and the circling of the fire.

B13C045.summary: Yudhishthira asks what should happen when a dowry-giver walks away from a marriage, and Bhishma answers with a set of rules on the girl's maintenance and on the rights of daughters and their sons. He cites the case of Savitri and an opinion of a king of Videha's line, and says a woman is never free. He then argues that a daughter sold for a price, or a dower taken for a daughter, is a sinful sale, and recites Yama's warning of punishment in hell for those who sell their children. The chapter treats marriage by sale as wrong.

scenes.B13C045S01: Yudhishthira's question on a jilted dowry-giver, Bhishma's rules on maintenance and inheritance by daughters and their sons, and his condemnation of sale in marriage.

shots.B13C045S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what the father or kinsmen should do when a man who gave a dowry walks away from the marriage.
